dhp221:1: One should abandon anger, one should abandon conceit,
dhp221:3: without clinging to mind and bodily form,
dhp221:4: sufferings never do befall the one having no possessions.
dhp222:1: Whoever should hold back arisen anger just like a swerving chariot,
dhp222:3: that one I say is a charioteer, other people are just rein-holders.
dhp223:1: Through kindness one should overcome anger, through goodness one should overcome a lack of goodness,
dhp223:3: through gifts one should overcome stinginess, through truth (one should overcome) lying speech.
dhp224:1: One should speak out the truth, one should not get angry, when requested give, if only a little,
dhp224:4: through these three conditions one can go to the presence of the gods.
dhp225:2: Those sages without violence, constantly restrained in body,
dhp225:3: go to the deathless (Nibbāna), having gone there they do not grieve.
dhp226:2: For those who are always wakeful, who train both by day and by night,
dhp226:4: who are intent on Nibbāna, the pollutants are laid to rest.
dhp227:2: This is something of old, Atula, this is not something of today:
dhp227:3: they blame the one who sits silently, they blame the one who talks a lot,
dhp227:5: they blame the one who talks in moderation, there is no one in the world not blamed.
dhp228:1: There was not and there will not be, and at present there is not found
dhp228:3: a person totally blameworthy, or one totally praiseworthy.
dhp229:1: The one who, after being examined day by day, is praised by the wise,
dhp229:3: faultless in conduct, sagacious, attending to virtue and wisdom,
dhp230:2: one who is like a golden coin, who is there worthy to blame him?
dhp230:3: That one is praised by the gods, and has been praised by the Brahmās too.
dhp231:1: One should guard against bodily anger, one should be restrained bodily,
dhp231:3: abandoning wrong bodily conduct, one should have good bodily conduct.
dhp232:1: One should guard against verbal anger, one should be restrained verbally,
dhp232:4: abandoning wrong verbal conduct, one should have good verbal conduct.
dhp233:1: One should guard against mental anger, one should be restrained mentally,
dhp233:3: abandoning wrong mental conduct, one should have good mental conduct.
dhp234:1: The wise are restrained bodily, then they are restrained verbally,
dhp234:3: the wise are restrained mentally, they are indeed very well-restrained.
dhp234:5: The Chapter about Anger, the Seventeenth
